summary: **Noting council seat duties and supplement correction**

item.text:
For a moment, you silently wonder whether your aunt once kept a blue glass bird on her desk. The thought remains only a guess. You give it no voice, and nothing in the library answers it.

Your attention returns to chapter five.

The book distinguishes obligations imposed by the Covenant from customs accumulated afterward. Every seat owes attendance, formal notice of succession, protection of accredited envoys, and disclosure of treaties that bind another signatory people. Designated heirs may observe selected Council sessions but hold no vote unless granted an emergency delegation.

The human seat acquired additional duties by custom. It chaired disputes involving incompatible magical traditions, certified translations where one language lacked the necessary legal concepts, and maintained records of cross-racial precedent.

An old training requirement expects a human heir to demonstrate working knowledge of two nonhuman magical disciplines before completing the Conclave course. A later hand has drawn a thin line through the paragraph and written *suspended during the vacancy* in the margin.

Across the room, Caelindra reaches the end of another chapter.

“Vauldren has crossed the glacier without boots,” she says. “He has also dismissed his guide for being pessimistic.”

Seraphel closes her eyes.

“He’s lost all his luggage, his mule, and his guide;  
At least if he freezes, he’ll finish with pride.”

“That is enough Vauldren for one evening.”

They gather the travel journal and empty teacups. Neither interrupts you as they leave.

Professor Stone remains at his desk. When he rises to replace a reference book, he notices which page lies open before you.

“The magical curriculum listed there was already obsolete when I was a student,” he says. “The grey supplement has the current requirements.”

He returns to his work.

At the bottom of the page, the next section begins beneath a formal heading:

*THE HUMAN SEAT IN ARBITRATION AND CONCORDANCE.*
